Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the fish-control transfer instructions and references, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence—including both required moving-window views—before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll keep the candidate rationale and reusable lesson in the two required files.

The contracts confirm two mandatory pauses before editing: the visual diagnosis must be written first, and the bookshelf transfer must be logged if it informs the policy. I’m now comparing all four sampled rollouts, with special attention to the best finite result versus the most informative failure; the scores alone are nearly tied, so trajectory and force diagnostics will decide the mechanism.

All samples are semantic successes, so there is no literal failure sheet in the assigned evidence. I’m treating the highest-score repeated capture as the efficiency reference and the prefilled fastest/highest-effort capture as the informative tradeoff case. This is the closest evidence-backed comparison available, and I’ll state that limitation rather than inventing a failure.

The visual-first review shows a stable, self-propelled S-approach with an alternating caudal street in every top-down sheet; every assigned oblique sheet is a black render artifact, so none can support a new 3D-wake claim. Numerically, the water-relative axial recovery is the strongest sampled controller (`23.424515T`, mean distance `2.184349L`, score `-0.287480`), while the independently tested adverse-yaw-moment residual also improves the prefill (`23.545517T`, `2.188316L`, `-0.291201`) without increasing peak force or moment. I’ll test their composition as one compact mechanism combination.

The bookshelf consultation now directly influences the edit: I’m translating its “slow route request versus fast disturbance residual” invariant into a small, target-opposition-gated posterior moment reflex. The notes will explicitly separate that invariant from nontransferable gains, exact vortex phase, geometry, and routes; the candidate will retain the strongest sampled water-relative carrier unchanged.

The candidate now contains exactly the planned composition: no gains were tuned, the strongest relative-flow carrier is preserved, and only the independently evidenced target-opposing moment residual was added to the posterior target. I’m now updating the durable experience bank with the completed parent result and the matched moment-residual result, while marking their composition as unverified until the next CFD evaluation.

The reusable lesson now records both completed semantic improvements, their exact performance/load envelopes, and the untested-composition boundary. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated non-CFD check runner now; while it validates guidance, schema, and edit boundaries, I’ll independently review the final diff and policy symmetry/finite-output behavior.

The configured check-runner could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account. I’m applying the safe fallback: the same three commands will be run exactly as specified—once by a general checker and once locally if needed—without CFD.

The first guidance check found a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one parent even though the guidance change is substantive. The contract says to repair and rerun, so I’m removing only the duplicated parent marker; this does not alter the experiment or candidate.

The fallback checker raced the README repair: its policy and boundary checks passed, but it captured the duplicate-parent failure just before that duplicate was removed. My local rerun now passes; I’m having the same checker rerun the repaired guidance check so the invoked check sequence finishes cleanly.

All required checks now pass after the duplicate marker repair: the guidance update is material, the policy returns two finite accelerations with a complete parameter schema, and the boundary check confirms only the allowed solver file changed. I’m doing one final non-CFD reflection-equivalence probe because the new moment gate couples turn sign and yaw-moment sign; this catches the main semantic risk in that composition.

Completed exactly one target-policy candidate.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl): combines water-relative locomotor recovery with bounded target-opposing yaw-moment rejection.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md): records visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md): materially updated with reusable evidence from the sampled results.

All non-CFD checks pass: guidance provenance, parameter schema and finite output, reflection equivalence, and editable-file boundary. No CFD was run.
